query: For boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment, what single intervention could improve resistance to molten-aluminum corrosion? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, defines the conditions under which it should remain effective, cites supporting prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment whose results could falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a modest amount of molybdenum (Mo) during the boriding process will enhance the molten-aluminum corrosion resistance of boride-based components used in hot-dip aluminum-plating equipment.
generation.material_initial_state: Standard boride-based component having a surface boride layer formed without Mo doping
generation.intervention: Incorporate controlled Mo-doping into the boriding treatment to form a Mo-enriched, protective boride layer
generation.conditions: Operated under typical hot-dip aluminum-plating conditions where the components are repeatedly exposed to molten aluminum at high temperatures
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a denser, more chemically stable Mo-doped boride phase on the surface
generation.mechanism: The addition of Mo enhances the passivation and stability of the boride layer by reducing the dissolution kinetics in molten aluminum, thereby decreasing corrosion rates. This is analogous to previous observations where Mo improved passivation properties in high-temperature alloys.
generation.predicted_outcome: The Mo-doped boride layer will exhibit a lower corrosion rate and improved integrity compared to the undoped baseline, leading to extended service life of the component under molten-aluminum exposure.
generation.baseline: Boride-based components prepared via conventional boriding without Mo doping
generation.boundary: The beneficial effect is expected as long as the Mo content is maintained within an optimal doping range and the operating temperature does not exceed the stability window for the Mo-doped boride phase.
generation.uncertainty: The exact Mo concentration required for optimal corrosion resistance and the quantitative improvement in corrosion rate remain to be determined experimentally.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of identically shaped boride-based components: one set processed with the standard boriding treatment and the other with the addition of a controlled amount of Mo during boriding. Expose both sets to molten aluminum under conditions mimicking hot-dip aluminum plating (temperature, time, and chemical environment). After exposure, perform comparative analyses using weight loss measurements, electrochemical tests (e.g., corrosion current density), and surface/microstructural characterization (e.g., SEM, EDS, XRD).
measurements: Electrochemical corrosion parameters (e.g., corrosion current density)
Surface microstructure and phase composition analyses
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Mo-doped components do not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in corrosion rate or improved surface integrity compared to the undoped baseline under all tested conditions, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: It was found that, by reducing the Mn concentration (to 5 at.% Mn), the CoCrFeMnNi alloy acquires higher yield strength values after annealing at 1117 K (from 387 to 477 MPa) due to the grain refinement effect (from 4.4 to 2.61 µm) []. Mn also shows a rapid evaporation effect during melting processes; hence, in our study, this element was replaced by Mo, which could improve the resistance to high temperatures []. Co–Cr–Mo alloy is widely used for manufacturing of vanes and gas turbines due to its excellent fatigue behavior and wear resistance [,,,]. In such alloys, molybdenum has a beneficial effect on passivation capacity, contributing to the formation of a protective surface layer that allows pitting corrosion to be limited [,]. Studies were conducted to estimate the effects on the microstructure and properties of alloys with different Mo contents [,,]. Such alloys have been designed for the manufacture of furnace casings and chemical tanks used in high-temperature and corrosion conditions [], for components used in the geothermal industry [,], or to obtain high-performance coatings [].

In this study, a reinforced layer was prepared on the surface of HEA by powder-pack boriding and focused on the effect of temperature and duration on the boronizing of CoCrFeNiMn HEA. The boronized samples were characterized using various methods. Furthermore, the properties of boronized CoCrFeNiMn alloys and diffusion behavior were investigated. This study could provide a reference for high hardness and high wear resistance HEA that could be used in a variety of industrial applications, such as the mold and crucible used in the cast aluminum industry [,], because the borides formed on the surface have high hardness, excellent corrosion resistance, and wear resistance [,], which allow HEA to be applied in special environments to increase service life.
